## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Paripuṇṇadvādasavassa-asikkhita-gihigata* is the sixty-sixth rule in the *Pācittiya* section of the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* [SuttaCentral]. The rule establishes that a nun incurs an offense requiring confession if she ordains a married girl who has completed twelve years of age but has not finished the required two-year training period [SuttaCentral; Hüsken 1997]. In her study of the Theravāda nun's Vinaya, Ute Hüsken notes that the canonical background narrative details the conferral of the training agreement (*sikkhāsammuti*), which must precede the two-year probationary period as a *sikkhamānā* [Hüsken 1997]. While the canonical rule explicitly requires the married girl to have reached twelve years of age before receiving permission to train in the six rules, the commentary in the *Samantapāsādikā* states that this permission may be granted to a married girl as young as ten, silently smoothing over a canonical discrepancy [Hüsken 1997]. An English translation of the rule and its commentary has been published by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

Direct parallels to this rule are preserved in the Pali *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* (Pc 66) and *Bhikkhunī Parivāra* (Pc 66), as well as in the Chinese translation of the Mahāsāṅghika *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* (Pc 102) and its *Pātimokkha*, and the Sanskrit Lokottaravāda *Bhikṣuṇī Vibhaṅga* (Pc 102) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus records substantial text reuse between this text and other Vinaya passages, most prominently adjacent ordination rules within the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* (such as Pc 67, Pc 72, Pc 73, Pc 63, Pc 64, and Pc 75) and various *Khandhakas* governing formal legal procedures and the nun's community (Kd 11, Kd 13, Kd 14, Kd 15, and Kd 20) [DharmaNexus]. Textual reuse is also traced in subcommentarial literature including the *Vinayasaṅgaha-aṭṭhakathā* and *Vinayavinicchayaṭīkā*, alongside cross-language alignments with the Tibetan *Bhikṣuṇīvinayavibhaṅga* (D0005), the Sanskrit *Pāṇḍulohitakavastu*, and the Tibetan *Vinayasūtra* [DharmaNexus].
